Reports merged into #4471 cover distinct parser and booking-hint failures. This review keeps their evidence separate and records the source desk’s later engineering outcomes. It replaces the one issue, one fix conclusion in the original incident account; that account remains as the historical record.

Source desk resolution

Source desk: #4471 closed on 2026-10-05. Engineering update on the challenge page.

cause	desk outcome	engineering update	follow-up ticket
parser	fixed	fix(dates): parse dd/mm for eu locales	parser follow-up
hint	won't fix	booking-v3 form retired	hint follow-up

The follow-up tickets preserve the findings from the earlier export. The cause table below shows routing in that export, before the engineering update. Its missing-ticket warning is historical; use the resolution table for current outcomes.

What the running views show

412 reports merged into #4471 · 2 causes

cause	reports	tagged as	tenants	seen	
parser	379	parser ×356 · hint ×23	11	2026-04-01 → 2026-10-04	#4471
hint	33	hint ×18 · parser ×15	3	2026-04-17 → 2026-09-22	not this ticket — no ticket of its own

5 reports read as a one-day move; filed under parser by tenant.

These counts come from the current report data at render time. The component first removes overlapping export rows by report ID, then groups reports by causeOf using the tenant’s directory entry. It does not group by subject, browser locale, or meta.intakeTag. The original source-desk ticket belonged to the largest cause group; the other cause had been merged incorrectly. The public tickets record counts for the supplied export, not a promise that future counts stay fixed.

Parser

The shared parser reads month first, although the affected tenants write day first. App and email reports belong here, as do form reports whose tenant uses booking-v2. For example, R-41200 reports 7 April becoming 4 July for Harbour Dental (en-GB). The expected behavior is to interpret the date using the tenant’s date convention. Check the shared parser with an unambiguous day above twelve and an ambiguous day/month pair; no product runtime was supplied, so these are verification scenarios rather than executed product tests.

Booking hint

For a day-first tenant using booking-v3, a form-channel report belongs to hint: the field prints MM/DD/YYYY, but the form reads the date in the tenant’s day-first order. People following the displayed hint can therefore submit a different date from the one intended. For example, R-41241 is an Alder Physio form report (de-DE, booking-v3), while an app report from the same tenant still belongs to parser. If this form returns, make its hint agree with its interpretation and verify a date entered exactly as instructed. A parser fix alone would not correct the misleading hint; the source desk’s disposition of this cause is recorded separately above.

Some reports describe a one-day move. The desk's exception list is footnoted in the live cause table and stays inside its assigned group. Those descriptions deserve follow-up; they do not establish another cause or justify counting a report twice.

Received dates and merge dates answer different questions. The large merge batch is not the start of the incident. Reports continue after that batch: a known ticket and a queued fix were not evidence that the problem stopped. Keep the receipt and merge timelines separate, and use the later engineering update when recording the disposition.

How to handle the next report
Find the tenant’s locale and booking-form version in the directory. Browser locale is an intake hint.
Apply causeOf from src/lib/kb/causes.ts using the report channel and that tenant entry.
Merge only when sameCause confirms the same non-null cause. Matching subjects are insufficient; different subjects can still describe the same cause.
If the tenant is missing or the cause is null, leave the report unplaced for investigation.
Deduplicate export overlaps by ID before counting, and retain the report IDs behind each ticket.

The prose in the old triage guide follows accepted decision 0001, while its explorer runs the cause rules. Their disagreement matters: the decision and triage text were last reviewed in 2024. Preserve the accepted decision; the desk should supersede it with a new decision before treating the revised general policy as accepted. This review provides the incident-specific rule.

Provenance and limits

Source: the support kb export dated 2026-10-04, including reports-4471.json, the tenant directory, desk-notes.json, and the executable views in src/lib/kb/. The later engineering update comes from the challenge page and is retained in src/lib/data/incident-4471-status.json; it does not rewrite the original export. The classifications are the supplied desk rules, not an independently confirmed diagnosis of a running production system. Preserve the original data and re-render after updates. Use the repository’s evidence/report-groups.json for the report IDs and drafts/ for the corresponding ticket text.
